newsitem.title: CHINA: China's B share indices end year up on rise hopes.
newsitem.headline: China's B share indices end year up on rise hopes.

text.p: China's B-share indices ended the Year of the Rat on a strong note by closing sharply higher on Friday, the last session before the Chinese Lunar New Year.
Brokers said the strong finish was in anticipation of a bullish Year of the Ox to come.
Shanghai's B share index jumped 1.065 points, or 1.62 percent, to 66.849 points, and Shenzhen's B index rose 2.6 points, or 1.68 percent, to 157.06.
China's stock exchange in Shanghai and Shenzhen will be closed for the Chinese Lunar New Year market holiday from Monday, February 3 until Monday, February 17.
"Investors were optimistic about most firms' 1996 results, many of which are expected to be released soon after the holiday," a Shenzhen broker said.
Most listed firms benefited from China's two cuts in bank interest rates last year, brokers said.
"Window-dressing buying supported the market with investors believing the market will go forward with overseas funds flowing in after the new year break," one Shanghai broker said.
In Shanghai, Industrial Sewing Machine Co Ltd rose strongly on speculative buying, gaining $0.008, or 4.76 percent, to $0.176 on volume of 51,000 shares.
Market barometer property developer Lujiazui followed on window-dressing buying by institutions, rising $0.036, or 4.37 percent, to $0.858 on volume of two million shares.
Huaxin Cement was the most active share on institutional buying on talk of improved 1996 results, gaining $0.006, or 2.12 percent, to $0.288 on volume of 2.5 million shares.
Southern Glass, the strongest performer in the B-share market, was the most active counter on volume of 3.67 million shares and rose HK$0.28, or 5.89 percent, to HK$5.03.
The rise was due in part to expectations that a 1.2 billion yuan float glass project would bring it substantial profits, brokers said.
Jiangling Motors was the second biggest gainer and added HK$0.17, or five percent, to HK$3.57 on trade of 868,350 shares.

Brokers said they expected the company to report sharply higher earnings for 1996 because U.S. giant Ford Co spent around US$40 million buying 80 percent of Jiangling's 174 million B shares in 1995 and introduced new technology to its plant.
On the A share markets, the indicies in Shanghai and Shenzhen moved up modestly with most investors staying on the sidelines in the last session before the new year, brokers said.
Shanghai's A index inched up 4.425 points, or 0.44 percent, to 1,006.362 points.
Chengdu People's Store was the star performer on buying late in the session, closing up 0.70 yuan, or 5.69 percent, to 13 yuan on volume of 1.4 million shares.

Shenzhen's A index gained 0.19 points, or 0.05 percent, to end at 372.54, with investor confidence strengthened by institutional buying in market giant Shenzhen Development Bank, brokers said. The counter advanced 0.26 yuan to 19.24 yuan on 27.15 million shares.

Inner Mongolia Yuanxing Natural Soda Co Ltd, which listed 58.5 million A shares in Shenzhen on Friday, ended the session at 11.70 yuan compared with an offer price of 5.11 yuan earlier this month. Volume was a heavy 41 million shares.
